headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 9 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.77 (95% CI: 0.63–0.95), suggesting that alcohol is associated with a lower risk of kidney and renal pelvis cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 88.70%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

sample_size.excerpt: Associations between alcohol intake up until study enrollment (prediagnosis) and risk of metachronous cancer were estimated using 9435 participants in the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study who were diagnosed with their first invasive cancer after enrollment (1990-1994).

effect_size.excerpt: We observed positive associations (per 10 g/d increment) for metachronous colorectal (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 1.00-1.14), upper aero-digestive tract (UADT) (HR = 1.16, 95% CI = 1.00-1.34) and kidney cancer (HR = 1.24, 95% CI = 1.10-1.39). Although these findings were partly explained by effects of smoking, the association for kidney cancer remained unchanged when current smokers or obese individuals were excluded.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: A U-shaped relationship between alcohol consumption and kidney cancer risk was observed among individuals with normoglycemia (light-to-moderate: HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99 and heavy: HR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.09, respectively).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: light-to-moderate: HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99 and heavy: HR, 1.00
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the effect and 95% CI using a two-sided Wald test on the log scale.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: A U-shaped relationship between alcohol consumption and kidney cancer risk was observed among individuals with normoglycemia (light-to-moderate: HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99 and heavy: HR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.09, respectively).
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Incident Kidney and renal pelvis cancer
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: light-to-moderate: HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99 and heavy: HR, 1.00

studies.Reference: Light to Moderate Alcohol Consumption and Cancer Incidence: The Norwegian Women and Health Cohort Study.
studies.Authors: Llaha F, Licaj I, Sharashova E, Ferrari P, Lukic M, Benjaminsen Borch K
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: In the NOWAC FFQs, women were asked whether they were alcohol abstainers; if not, they were asked about their average frequency consumption of wine, beer, spirits, and liqueurs during the past 12 months.

sample_size.excerpt: Participants were 70,932 women aged 41–70 years, randomly recruited in the Norwegian Women and Health (NOWAC) cohort study from 1996 to 2004.
sample_size.location: Materials and Methods > Study Population, paragraph 1

cases.excerpt: During a mean follow-up of 19 years, 254 women developed pancreatic cancer, 226 kidney cancer, 1,378 colorectal cancer, 1,001 lung cancer, 1,531 of postmenopausal breast cancer, 214 of postmenopausal ovarian cancer, and 346 of postmenopausal endometrial cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: For kidney cancer, the estimated HR from each additional 12g/day of alcohol consumption was 0.42 (95% CI = 0.24 to 0.75, Figure 2 ). This pattern of association was also observed across subgroup analyses, but with some differences in precision and magnitude.

confidence_interval.excerpt: For kidney cancer, the estimated HR from each additional 12g/day of alcohol consumption was 0.42 (95% CI = 0.24 to 0.75, Figure 2 ).

comparison.excerpt: For kidney cancer, the estimated HR from each additional 12g/day of alcohol consumption was 0.42 (95% CI = 0.24 to 0.75, Figure 2 ).

design.excerpt: Participants were 70,932 women aged 41–70 years, randomly recruited in the Norwegian Women and Health (NOWAC) cohort study from 1996 to 2004.

timing.excerpt: For each woman, we computed person-years of follow-up starting from the age at baseline until the attenuated age of diagnosis of any type of cancer, emigration, death, or end of study on 31 December 2020, whichever came first.
timing.location: Materials and Methods > Statistical Analysis, paragraph 3

continent.excerpt: Shortly, 172,478 women were randomly recruited across Norway during 1991–2007.
